fertilizer.nutrient_principles: Focus on Nitrogen for maximum tiller production and Phosphorus for strong root and shoot development. Zinc is critical in submerged conditions.
fertilizer.timing_guidance: Apply first top dressing at 20-25 DAT, second at 40-45 DAT if required
fertilizer.notes: Zinc deficiency is common in submerged rice. Apply zinc sulfate at 25 kg/ha or 0.5% foliar spray if deficiency observed.
fertilizer.risk_if_skipped: Reduced tillering, weak canopy, and poor yield potential
fertilizer.soil_type_adjustment: For light-textured sandy soils, split nitrogen into 3-4 doses; for heavy clay soils, 2-3 splits are adequate.
fertilizer.deficiency_symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaves (N), reduced tillering, stunted height, purple tinge on older leaves (P), leaf bronzing (Zn)
fertilizer.avoid_overuse: Avoid applying all nitrogen as basal. Excessive vegetative growth from over-fertilization increases lodging and disease risk.
fertilizer.weather_precautions: Apply fertilizer when soil is moist and no heavy rain is expected. Avoid application during continuous overcast or waterlogged conditions.
fertilizer.recommended_focus: Nitrogen and phosphorus support for maximum tiller production and canopy development
fertilizer.organic_alternatives: Green manuring with dhaincha or sunn hemp incorporated before transplanting. Apply well-decomposed compost at 10-15 tons/ha.
fertilizer.cost_efficiency_tip: Use leaf color chart (LCC) for need-based nitrogen application to reduce costs by 20-25% while maintaining yield.

fertilizer.cost_efficiency_tip: Apply potassium based on soil test results to avoid over-application. Muriate of potash (MOP) is cost-effective and readily available.
